# Report structure (generated by `render` from reviewed.json)

Rendering is deterministic: your job is to write a good reviewed.json. This file shows what each section should look like so the content lands in the right place.

```
# Literature Radar · 2026-09-16 (Wednesday) · Daily
> Window 2026-09-15 -> 2026-09-16 · Sources: arxiv / biorxiv / openalex / europepmc · Fetched 512 -> deduplicated 447 -> queued 19 -> recommended 3
> WARNING - failed sources: europepmc (today's coverage is incomplete)     <- only when something failed

## At a glance
**headline: one sentence with today's most important signal**
signal: what the candidate pool says, which directions were active or quiet (1-3 sentences)
Top three to read first:
1. **Original title** - one-line reason

## ★★★ Must read (score >= 85)
### 1. [Original title](url)
- Authors et al. · venue · date · article type · (preprint, not peer reviewed)
- DOI [10.xxx](https://doi.org/10.xxx) · arXiv:xxxx
- **Score 88.5** ★★★ · relevance 95 / novelty 80 / quality 85 / methodology 90 / inspiration 85 · evidence: abstract/full text verified · STRONG RECOMMENDATION
- **Why you should read it**: <= 60 words, pointing at a specific manuscript
- **For a general ecologist**: 80-160 words, plain language, no equations
- **Core findings**: 3-5 bullets
- **Links to your work**:
  - [project-a] Project label from the profile - which section / which derivation
- **Reviewer's eye**: 1-2 bullets
- **Terms**: only in brief/dual mode and only when needed
- Needs verification: ...
- Suggested action: read-full · Tags: #tag-one #tag-two

## ★★ Worth a look (score 70-84)
(same layout, may be shorter)

## Peripheral scan (below the recommendation threshold, one line each)
- [Original title](url) · venue · date - one line an outside colleague can read
  - For a general ecologist: optional short explanation

## Theme pulse
- theme clusters (one sentence each)
- (continuity) links to the research memory

## Testable research ideas
1. idea / how to test / related papers

## Search log
- per-source counts and status, dedup and queue statistics, exclusions, weights and thresholds
```

## How to write each part

**headline**: like a message to a busy colleague. "A preprint extends the core mechanism to the setting your chapter 3 studies" is good; "19 candidates were retrieved today" is not (statistics belong in the log).

**signal**: directions, not counts. Say it when a day is quiet: "Nothing new on the core theme today; two empirical papers on the secondary theme, neither with the dimension you care about."

**Why you should read it**: the subject is the user. "Your manuscript criticises method X; this paper supplies the counter-example" beats "This paper compares two methods".

**For a general ecologist** (heading kept for all fields; it means "for a colleague outside the sub-field"): the question, what was done and its scope, the qualitative result, why it matters. No equations; gloss unavoidable terms inline; state whether the result is analytical, simulated or empirical. This paragraph is required for every recommended paper.

**Core findings**: start with a verb, carry the condition. "In the weak-noise limit the effect grows linearly with the correlation time (numerical only)" beats "Studied the effect of noise". Copy numbers exactly and say where they come from (abstract / text / figure).

**Links to your work**: every item maps onto an `active_projects` key and says where it is used: citation location, argument to answer, simulation to reproduce, derivation technique to borrow.

**Reviewer's eye**: the Major concern you would raise as a referee; no pleasantries.

**Peripheral one-liners**: what it did, then why it missed the cut ("no mechanism", "numerics only", "off-topic but the method is borrowable").

**Research ideas**: must be testable - name the data / model / derivation that would test it, and what it would mean if it holds or fails.

**Zero-recommendation days**: `articles: []`, `summary.headline` says so plainly, fill peripheral (<= 10), and use the theme pulse to explain why it was quiet (holiday, indexing lag, a low-output direction).

## Weekly / catch-up differences

- Theme pulse grows to 3-6 items and aggregates candidates by theme instead of paper by paper.
- `continuity_notes` look back at the research memory's tag totals for the last 4 weeks and name trends.
- The recommendation cap stays at 10; the rest goes to peripheral (up to 15 if listed explicitly; `render` truncates at `max_peripheral`, so raise it in the profile when needed).
